details:
Q1: Should merged PRs from `claude/*` head branches (interactive Claude Code sessions) still count as an authorized source once the new base and same-repository checks pass?
Choices:
A) Yes. Keep `claude/*` authorized, but also require `base.ref` equal to the sync base (`BASE_BRANCH`, default `main`), `head.repo.full_name` equal to this repository, and the author check from Q2. Anything else is held as a draft PR. (RECOMMENDED)
B) No. Add `claude/` to the pipeline-head pattern so every `claude/*`-sourced template change goes to the held draft PR for human review, along with the base and repository checks.
C) Make it configurable with a new env var (default: same as A) so operators can hold `claude/*` sources without a code change.
Q2: What counts as "approved provenance" for the merged PR's author and commits?
Choices:
A) The PR's `author_association` (already in the existing `commits/{sha}/pulls` response, so no extra API call) must be `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`. Bot accounts (`user.type == "Bot"` or a `[bot]` login) are held. The existing PR-commit subject and marker checks stay as they are. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Same as A, and also require every PR commit's GitHub-resolved `author.login` (already in the existing `pulls/{n}/commits` response) to be non-null, not a bot, and equal to the PR author or another trusted login. Commits with an unresolved or mismatched author are held.
C) Require the PR author to be on an explicit allowlist from a new env var (default: the repository owner only). All other authors are held.
